title: Biolistic Transformation of Eutreptiella gymnastica and Pyramimonas parkeae Using Gene Gun
author: Anna Vanclová and Vladimír Hampl
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ibvcan6
materials: Particles were delivered by PDS-1000/He (Bio-Rad) on 1250 psi, with 6 cm distance between the macrocarrier and the plate.

steps.title: Prepare cell suspensions on agar
steps.instruction: Harvest 1–5 × 10⁶ cells of Eutreptiella gymnastica and Pyramimonas parkeae (or 1–5 × 10⁸ cells of B. natans), make thick suspensions, and layer them onto agar plates immediately before bombardment.

steps.title: Coat gold particles with DNA
steps.instruction: Using organism‑specific gold particles (1 µm for E. gymnastica; 0.6 µm for P. parkeae and B. natans), coat each batch with 5 µg of the appropriate plasmid (Eutre‑PACLUC, Pyr‑G418LUC, or Bigelo‑G418LUC) and label the particles with fluorescein via the Mirus Label‑IT system. Keep DNA, coated particles, and DNA‑treated cells protected from light.

steps.title: Bombard cells with DNA‑coated particles
steps.instruction: Load each agar‑plate sample into the gene gun and fire the DNA‑coated gold particles onto the cells. Immediately after bombardment, transfer the cells to fresh growth media.

steps.title: Incubate before antibiotic selection
steps.instruction: Allow the cultures to sit undisturbed for several hours in the dark, then add the appropriate antibiotic: 10 µg ml⁻¹ puromycin for E. gymnastica, or 400 µg ml⁻¹ geneticin for P. parkeae and B. natans.

steps.title: Fix cells for microscopy
steps.instruction: Withdraw 1 ml of cells from each sample, fix with 1 % formaldehyde, and mount onto a microscope slide using Vectashield mounting medium.

steps.title: Cultivate fixed cells
steps.instruction: Incubate the mounted slides for 14 days at 18–20 °C under a 12‑hour light/12‑hour dark cycle.
